about.title: Norwalk Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Norwalk residents get their care from a mix of neighborhood clinics, urgent care offices, and larger Los Angeles County hospitals a short drive away. When something goes wrong, the questions come fast: Was this a known risk, or did someone miss something they should have caught? California law draws that line carefully. A disappointing result on its own is not malpractice; the claim turns on whether a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and whether that lapse actually caused harm. Proving it almost always takes a qualified medical expert reviewing the records. Timing matters too. Under MICRA you generally have one year from when you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from when it happened, and a 90-day notice must go to the provider before a lawsuit is filed. Our team handles malpractice cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: MICRA's clock runs on discovery, not the calendar
items.desc: Many patients in Norwalk don't realize something went wrong until months later. We can pin down when your one-year discovery window opened and whether the three-year outer limit still leaves room to act.

items.title: The 90-day notice is handled correctly
items.desc: California requires written notice to the provider before a malpractice suit is filed. We build that step into the timeline so a paperwork issue doesn't cost you the claim.

items.title: Expert review before anyone makes promises
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone is not malpractice, a qualified medical expert nearly always has to confirm the standard of care was breached. We line that review up early and are candid if the case isn't there.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on Imperial Highway and the ER sent me home. Could that be malpractice?
items.answer: It can be, but only if the emergency staff fell below the accepted standard of care — for example, skipping imaging that a reasonable doctor would have ordered given your symptoms. In 2025, Norwalk recorded 546 people injured in traffic collisions, and many were seen in local emergency rooms, so this question comes up. We'll want your ER records and a medical expert's opinion before drawing any conclusion. Keep in mind you may also have a separate claim against the driver who caused the crash.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California places a cap on non-economic damages — things like pain and loss of enjoyment of life — and that cap increases every year under current MICRA law. Economic losses such as medical bills and lost income are not subject to that cap. We can explain which figure applies based on when your case resolves.

items.question: Do you charge Norwalk residents anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. Our team provides a free case review, and we work on contingency, meaning we collect a fee only if there is a recovery in your case.
